T4.title: 51169's cause is FOUND — NOM is above Binance's platform-wide Maximum Collateral Limit
T4.root_cause: Binance enforces a platform-wide, per-asset Maximum Collateral Limit shared across ALL users, explicitly covering Portfolio Margin. Above 100% utilisation, buying or transferring that asset into a margin account is blocked with no exceptions. NOM is above 100%: the user's Binance app reports a maximum transfer-in/buy quantity of 0. The collateral capacity available for additional NOM is therefore zero, which is literally what MARGIN_TRADE_COEFF_INSUFFICIENT describes.
T4.how_it_was_found: The user attempted a NOM transfer-in and a NOM buy by hand in the Binance app on 2026-07-28 and reported the refusal message verbatim; the bookkeeper then confirmed the mechanism against Binance's official FAQ.
T4.user_observed_message_verbatim: 代币NOM已达平台抵押金额上限。最大入/买入数量为0。请调低数量或使用其他代币重试。
T4.also_explains: The 2026-07-27 asymmetry — the UM perpetual SELL needs no NOM collateral and filled; the margin BUY needs it and was blocked.

T4.product_followup_out_of_scope: Any coin above its collateral cap is structurally un-hedgeable in the forward direction while the cap holds, and there is no documented way to know before trying. Surfacing that on the opportunity table, or remembering it per-coin with an expiry, is a product question beyond this stage.

harness_followups.key_finding: AGENTS.md's raw-artifact requirement binds REVIEWERS only ('Reviewers are read-only. They must inspect raw artifacts'). Whole-file 必読 lists in implementation packets are therefore a convention we adopted, not a contract requirement — so narrowing them needs no contract amendment. Packets state an expected reading budget and instruct the session to report if it is blowing past it, rather than discovering it at 65%.
